questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Exploring new cultures and getting new perspectives on political science through a wide variety of courses that were provided at UBC. 

Canada is an interesting state in the way it has to balance its colonial history as well as separatist movements in Alberta and Quebec.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of British Columbia has been very accommodating for exchange students. They provided extensive tools/arrangements for meeting other internationals and overall making my stay an interesting and fruitful experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: General information on the University's system at UBC from professors and TA's. General information of all the student clubs. General information of the University's facilities as well as ways of getting help (medical, practical, or student program specific.).

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. I managed to find accomodation through AirBnB with some friends and random students from Facebook. Was cheap enough but in hindsight I would have also considered staying at a hostel for a bit until I found a room with some locals in Vancouver. I think that would have been a more interesting cultural experience.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you are pretty much guaranteed a room on campus as a Go Global Exchange Student. I was first rejected for a room but got a room 2 months before my departure but then I had made other arrangements. Trust the process.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Information available was a little bit confusing. You have to pay to be on the waitlist and as soon as I had payed I recieved a mail that said I didn't get a room... That was confusing and it would have been nice to know that I was pretty much guaranteed a room as an exchange student.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. You get 2 weeks of "trying" different courses that you had preselected and then you commit to the ones you want. Some of the professors expressed dissatisfaction with the system but I found it helpful to find the right courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As mentioned above. Get admitted to 6 courses and can later pick and choose or change all together (if you have the requisites for the courses.).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are offices with student counselling which I found to be helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make yourself familiar with the syllabus. All information needed can be found here, as they cover what the course entails extensively.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As a Danish MA student you can in theory take MA courses but it requires a lengthy process of getting approved by the professor at UBC. I was advised by UCPH to just take BA (1-300 level) courses. I will however suggest to stick to the 300 level courses as 100-200 courses seemed very introductory.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching differed massively. There were no group sessions for discussion in my courses so my courses were basically listening to a Ted Talk from the professors for 90 minutes straight. A bit of a culture shock at first but ended up enjoying them thoroughly as they were very in depth with specific topics. We did have class discussions WITH the professor, and everyone had the opportunity to ask questions throughout the lessons. Parcipitation and weekly tests count towards your grades, so you have to show up for all lectures and stay on top of the readings. The size of the curriculum differed quite a bit from course to course. One of my courses had about 150 pages a week, while another course only had about 50+ pages.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Consumers and Consumption (SOCI)
2) International Security: The Governance of Outer Space (POLI 369B)
3) Politics and Development (POLI 338B)
4) Chinese Politics and Development (POLI 321)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
2) International Security: The Governance of Outer Space (POLI 369B)
I had no idea how the current space race and the montization of space was forming international politics. Be prepared to familiarize yourself with international law and learn the legality of SpaceX's ambitions of putting 1 million satellites in space when collissions of satellites could render the Orbits of the Earth unusuable for centuries.

3) Politics and Development (POLI 338B)
Learn about how Foreign Aid is its own medium for power politics among the greates economic and military powers. Learning about the conditionalities of the IMF and China's BRI lending was truly interesting. Be prepared to read, as the readings are about 100-150 pages a week with difficult readings on the readings. Well worth the effort in my opinion.

questions.answer: They charge you for Student Medical Insurance even though you are covered by your own travel insurance. I managed to argue my way out of it but it took months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were expensive. Living cheap isn't easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a climber, skier/snowboarder/, hiker, surfer or just outdoor enthusiast there are loads of student societies that will make your stay fun!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Museums at campus, dance lessons, combat sport lessons drop-in sports and intramural sport tournaments.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join the UBC Outdoor Varsity Club and stay tuned for arranged trips.

Heard good things about the Surfing Society too but didn't have the time for it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Buy the season pass for Whistler ski resort well in advance (no later than late november) and go snowboarding!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: no issue at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Saying "How are you" all the time. Turned out to be one of my favorite aspects of my stay though as it allowed for loads of interactions with Canadians and other internationals.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendlyness and politeness. People for instance que up to take the bus and are expected to do the same if you don't want to piss off some Canadians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Take the Student Accomodation or stay at a hostel until you can find a room with some locals if you don't want to share a semi gross kitchen.
2) Stay on top of the readings. Falling behind and missing quizzes that count towards your grade is a bad idea.
3) Enjoy the outdoors as much as possible!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My courses were surprisingly interesting. But overall just getting experience with a North American University and Canadian culture was well worth the stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not spending all my money on fun stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
